title: P23C — one real Alembic downgrade of the head revision against a live database holding committed audited business, one real re-upgrade, and the honest cost of both
problem: P23A proved this system can lose its whole database and get the truth back out of an archive; P23B proved it can lose the node and carry on over a promoted copy. Both answer “the infrastructure failed”. Neither answers the failure every team actually meets more often: the schema change itself was wrong and has to come back out while the listener is running. Nobody in this repository had ever run one of its own revisions backwards against a database holding committed audited business. Whether the three earlier business tables and their rows survive it, whether the head revision's table, trigger, function, policy and runtime grant really go away or merely stop being named by alembic_version, whether a never-restarted listener meeting the older schema fails closed without leaking the credential it holds or leaving a customer row no decision ever authorised, whether going forward again restores every security property exactly, and what it costs the audit trail, were all unknown.
solution: One migration seam, tests/_harness/live-migration-rollback-probe.mjs, is added BESIDE the two P22 harnesses, the P23A recovery seam and the P23B failover seam and changes no byte of any of them. It starts no environment, defines no image, publishes no port on the served database and holds no environment of its own: it is handed the ONE P22B1 environment and reads the container names, the network, the data volume, the run's unique label and the pinned image out of it. It writes no schema statement at all — the repository's OWN revisions run in both directions through the SAME locked `uv run --frozen` toolchain the environment already migrates with. Because the isolated database publishes nothing, each migration happens in a maintenance window: the served container is stopped cleanly and removed while its named volume is left alone, the same volume is briefly re-served by a throwaway container bound to 127.0.0.1, the owning mfk_migration role is given a fresh one-shot password over the database's own trusted local socket with the statement on stdin, the revisions run with the URL on stdin, and the throwaway container is removed before the same volume is re-served under the original name, network and alias with no host port. Every HTTP request, verification read and trusted principal in the frozen test is the UNCHANGED P22B2 probe's.

the live environment really stands at the real head, and one trusted write commits there — four tables, one verified genesis decision, and the head revision's full security shape recorded from the server itself

the repository's OWN head revision really runs backwards against that live database — the three business tables and their committed rows survive untouched, while the rolled-back revision's table, trigger, function, policy and grant are gone and take the audited decision history with them

the never-restarted listener meets the older schema and fails closed — no receipt, no committed claim, no credential or connection string in the answer, and not one business row left behind that no decision ever authorised
the same revision re-applied brings the structure and every security property of it back exactly as they were — and brings back none of the destroyed rows

the audited business resumes on the re-applied schema through the never-restarted listener — as a NEW chain genesis beside the rows that survived — and teardown leaves zero labelled resources and no secret on disk

conditionalDeliveryGates.evidence: One problem only: when a schema change in this repository turns out to be wrong, can its own revision be run backwards against a live database holding committed audited business, what survives it, what it costs, and does the business resume when it is re-applied.

Three files, all new: the frozen test, one migration probe beside the two P22 harnesses and the P23A and P23B seams, and this manifest. No existing file is modified, and the five migration surfaces the package claims to reverse are asserted byte-identical.

The environment is the UNCHANGED P22B1 one, every HTTP request, verification read and trusted principal is the UNCHANGED P22B2 probe's, the revisions are the repository's own, and nothing P23A or P23B already proved is proved again here.

No schema statement written by the probe, no credential on a command line or in an environment value, no host port on the served database, a maintenance window bound to loopback and removed even on failure, bounded waits everywhere, redacted failures, and every claim read back from PostgreSQL or the daemon rather than from a descriptor.
The writer's single full local QA and the required CI full QA are the two allowed executions; both must be recorded before this gate turns GREEN.
A separate read-only Claude session on this immutable snapshot must accept the package: the writer never reviews what the writer wrote.
Delete the three new files; the labelled sweep the run already performs removes the re-served database, the maintenance container, the data volume, the built image tag and the host secret directory.

environmentPins.migrationToolchain: the repository's own revisions, run through the same locked `uv run --frozen` alembic the P22B1 environment already migrates with. A rollback proven by a differently resolved alembic is a rollback of a different program.
environmentPins.maintenanceCredentialDelivery: a fresh one-shot password minted per window, set over the database's own trusted local socket with the statement on stdin and handed to alembic in a URL on stdin. No value ever reaches an argument, an environment variable, docker inspect, a log or a returned descriptor, and it is forgotten the moment the window closes.

rollback.mechanism: Delete tests/_harness/live-migration-rollback-probe.mjs and planning/kernel-migration-rollback-p23c.json, and the frozen test if the whole package is withdrawn. Nothing else changes, because nothing else was touched.
rollback.blastRadius: Confined to one new test-only probe file plus this manifest and the frozen test. No src module, no host module, no image definition, no schema, no alembic revision, no migration module, no CI file and no dependency is involved, and the run's own labelled sweep removes the re-served database, the maintenance container, the data volume, the image tag and the host secret directory.
rollback.compensatingStepReason: Nothing outside the run survives it: the maintenance container carries the run's unique label and is removed by the seam in a finally block even when a migration fails, the re-served database and its volume are removed by the unchanged P22B1 teardown, and the seam writes no file to this host at all.

nonGoals: No zero downtime and no online migration: the listener is refused for the whole maintenance window, because the database it talks to is stopped, migrated and re-served while it keeps running.

No expand and contract and no backward compatible schema change: this package takes the head revision straight out and puts it straight back, which is exactly the shape a rollout designed to avoid an outage does not have.

No data migration and no data-migration rollback: nothing here moves, rewrites or back-fills a row, and the rows owned only by the rolled-back revision are destroyed by that revision's own reverse step and are never restored.
No automatic detection and no automatic rollback: nothing watches a migration, judges it or reverses it by itself, and every step is an operator's deliberate act inside one scenario.
No point-in-time recovery, no WAL archive and no backup schedule: P23A's verified archive stays the only backup this repository owns, and this package neither takes nor consults one.
No high availability, no failover and no second copy: the P23B standby is not started, contacted or referenced, and there is exactly one database node throughout.
No agreed RPO and no agreed RTO: this package measures no recovery objective, proposes none and negotiates none.

No production, no staging, no registry, no external deployment and no new image: the pinned P22A2 image and the P22B1 environment are used exactly as they are, no host port is opened on the served database, and no roadmap, release, version or CI surface is touched.
capabilityDelta: REAL_MIGRATION_ROLLBACK_AND_REUPGRADE: this system can now take its own head schema revision back out of a live database that already holds committed audited business, and put it back again, with the three earlier business tables and every one of their rows surviving both directions untouched and their security shape unchanged. The rollback is real — the revision's table, append-only trigger, function, tenant-isolation policy and runtime grant are gone from the server's own catalogues, not merely unnamed by alembic_version — the never-restarted listener fails closed against the older schema without leaking its credential or leaving an unauthorised row, and the re-applied revision comes back with row-level security enabled AND forced, the append-only trigger enforcing again even against the superuser, and exactly the two privileges the runtime role held before and no third one.

productClaim.runnable: The drill runs today: `node --test tests/kernel-migration-rollback-p23c.test.mjs` brings up the unchanged P22B1 environment at the real head, commits one trusted write over live HTTP, runs the repository's own head revision backwards through its own locked alembic, proves what survived and what did not, sends a write into the older schema and watches it fail closed, re-applies the revision, and commits a second audited write through the listener that was never restarted.
productClaim.notRunnable: There is still no runnable product. There is no user interface, no persistent or hosted environment, and nothing that detects a bad migration or reverses one without an operator. And the central finding is a cost, not a capability: this rollback DESTROYS the audited decision history, because the head revision's own reverse step drops the table that holds it, and re-applying the revision brings the structure back and not one of those audit rows. The chain resumes as a new genesis, so the system cannot prove afterwards what it decided before the rollback. A schema rollback over an audit table is an operational decision, never a routine one.

userJourney.once: Önceden bir şema değişikliği yanlış çıktığında ne olacağı bu depoda hiç denenmemişti. Elimizde sadece “yedekten dön” (P23A) ve “ikinci kopyaya geç” (P23B) vardı; ikisi de donanım veya sunucu arızası içindir. Yanlış olan şeyin şemanın kendisi olduğu durumda kimse geri alma adımını gerçek veriyle çalıştırmamıştı.
userJourney.simdi: Şimdi deponun kendi göç dosyaları, canlı ve içinde gerçek kayıt bulunan bir veritabanı üzerinde geriye doğru çalıştırılıyor, sonra tekrar ileriye alınıyor. Bakım penceresi sadece bu makineye açılıyor, hiçbir parola komut satırına veya ortam değişkenine yazılmıyor ve uygulama konteyneri hiç yeniden başlatılmıyor.
userJourney.fark: Fark ölçülebilir hale geldi. Müşteri, denetim ve giden-kutu tablolarındaki satırlar geri alma sırasında tek tek aynı kalıyor. Buna karşılık geri alınan sürümün kendi tablosu, tetikleyicisi, fonksiyonu, kuralı ve yetkisi gerçekten siliniyor — sadece sürüm numarası değişmiyor — ve o tablodaki karar geçmişi yok oluyor.
userJourney.kullaniciYolculugu: Bir CRM kullanıcısı müşteri formunu dolduruyor, kayıt oluşuyor ve arkasında bir denetim kaydı ile bir karar kaydı bırakıyor. Sonra operatör hatalı şema sürümünü geri alıyor. Bu pencerede kullanıcı formu tekrar gönderirse sessizce “kaydettim” yanıtı almıyor: açık bir hata dönüyor, yarım müşteri kaydı oluşmuyor ve hata mesajı ne parolayı ne de eksik tablonun adını gösteriyor. Operatör sürümü geri getirdiğinde kullanıcı formu yeniden gönderiyor, kayıt oluşuyor ve eski müşteri satırının yanına ekleniyor. Ancak karar geçmişi sıfırdan başlıyor: geri alma öncesindeki kararın kanıtı geri gelmiyor.
userJourney.kalanEngel: Kalan engel açık ve bu paketin asıl bulgusu: denetim tablosu üzerinde şema geri alma bedava değil. Geri alma o tablodaki karar geçmişini siliyor ve ileri alma onu geri getirmiyor, yani “daha önce neye izin verdik” sorusunun cevabı kayboluyor. Ayrıca bu bir kesintisiz göç değil: pencere boyunca sistem yazma kabul etmiyor, kimse hatalı göçü kendiliğinden fark etmiyor ve her adımı bir insan başlatıyor.

residualRisks: The rollback is destructive by the revision's own design. The frozen test asserts that destruction rather than working around it, so an operator reading this package is told the cost before they approve one; nothing here makes the cost smaller.
The window is a real outage. The database is stopped, migrated and re-served while the listener keeps running, so every write during the window fails — safely, but it fails.
One node, one host, one ephemeral environment. There is no second copy, no archive taken before the rollback and no monitoring, and the whole environment deletes itself at the end of the run.
